description: Verify that a valid authenticated user can access the protected /auth/me endpoint and receive their authenticated user profile.
rationale: A valid authentication token should be accepted and /auth/me should return the authenticated user's profile.

description: Verify that the authenticated identity returned by /auth/me matches the user associated with the authentication context.
rationale: A valid authentication token must resolve to the correct authenticated user and must not expose another user's identity.

description: Verify that a standard user cannot access another user's protected resource.
rationale: A standard user should not access another user's protected resource unless explicitly permitted.

description: Verify that an authenticated user can retrieve their own user resource using their valid user ID.
rationale: An authenticated user should be able to retrieve the user resource identified by their own valid user ID.

description: Verify that a standard user cannot delete another user's account.
rationale: A standard user should not be able to delete another user's account. A 403 response represents the expected production authorization boundary.

description: Verify that authorization is consistently enforced when a different standard user attempts to delete another user's account.
rationale: Authorization must be enforced consistently regardless of which standard user attempts to delete another user's account.

description: Verify that a standard user cannot modify another user's role or elevate another user's privileges.
owaspCategories: API3:2023 - Broken Object Property Level Authorization
rationale: A standard user must not be able to modify another user's authorization role or elevate another account's privileges.

description: Verify that a moderator cannot perform administrator-level account deletion against an administrator account.
rationale: A moderator should not have administrator-level privileges to delete user accounts.

description: Verify that a standard user cannot elevate their own privileges by changing their role to administrator.
owaspCategories: API3:2023 - Broken Object Property Level Authorization
rationale: A standard user must not be able to elevate their own privileges by changing their role to administrator.

description: Verify that an administrator can perform an authorized user-account deletion.
rationale: The administrator role is authorized to delete user accounts, while lower-privileged roles are expected to be denied. This test verifies that the administrative authorization boundary permits the intended operation.

description: Verify that requesting a non-existent user resource returns a safe not-found response.
rationale: A non-existent resource ID should fail safely with a not-found response and should not expose unnecessary information about the underlying data set.

description: Verify that a non-numeric user ID is rejected safely rather than causing an unhandled error or an unexpected match.
rationale: Not documented by DummyJSON. Stated expectation: a syntactically invalid identifier should fail safely with a client error (400) rather than a 200, or a 500 that could leak implementation detail such as a stack trace.

description: Verify that a negative, syntactically valid but semantically impossible user ID fails safely as not-found.
rationale: Not documented by DummyJSON. Stated expectation: a negative ID can never correspond to a real resource, so it should behave the same as any other non-existent ID (404), not surface a different or more permissive code path.

description: Verify that the authenticated user's profile does not expose sensitive personal, credential, or financial information.
owaspCategories: API3:2023 - Broken Object Property Level Authorization
rationale: The authenticated user resource should be retrievable, but sensitive fields such as passwords and other credential material must not be unnecessarily exposed. Sensitive-field validation is performed independently from the status assertion.
